name: All Terrain Vehicle
description: Any self-propelled vehicle manufactured for sale for use mainly on off-highway trails or in off-highway competition, no more than 70 inches wide or 1,000 pounds dry; it takes in off-road motorcycles, so an off-road e-moto is registered as one. Defined by Vehicle and Traffic Law §2281 and regulated by Article 48-C.
restrictions: Manufactured for use mainly on off-highway trails or in off-highway competition, no more than 70 inches wide or 1,000 pounds dry weight
Includes off-road motorcycles, whatever the motor
Registered with the DMV every year, expiring August 31, with a plate on the rear and a sticker on the right side
Must carry liability insurance to ride anywhere but the owner's own property
Riders under 14 must be supervised by an adult or ride on land their parent or guardian owns or leases; riders 14 and 15 also may ride alone once they finish a DMV-approved safety course
Riders and passengers must wear a protective helmet
Needs working brakes, a muffler, a US Forest Service–approved spark arrester, and lights from a half-hour after sunset
Ridden on a highway only where it's designated and posted open to ATVs; may cross other highways, but not interstates or controlled-access highways, at about a right angle after a full stop
On public lands only where designated and posted open to ATVs, and on private land only with the owner's consent
A dirt bike or mini-bike can't be registered or ridden on any street, highway, parking lot or sidewalk open to public motor vehicle traffic
